mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE first exceeds 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals an expansion in household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low unemployment rate below 4% for at least six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE stays below 4% for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth) without a corresponding rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a savings glut that depresses demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises month-over-month while GDPC1 does not
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises month-over-month without a corresponding rise in GDPC1.
